tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>

  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	"""Render a Claude Code session transcript (.jsonl) to readable Markdown, without editing content."""
2	import json, sys
3	
4	src, dst, title = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
5	out = [f"# {title}", "",
6	       f"Source: Claude Code session transcript `{src.split(chr(92))[-1]}` (raw JSONL included alongside).",
7	       "Rendered verbatim: user messages, assistant replies, tool calls and tool results in order. "
8	       "Internal harness records (request metadata, file snapshots) are omitted here but present in the raw JSONL.", ""]
9	
10	def text_of(content):
11	    if isinstance(content, str):
12	        return content
13	    parts = []
14	    for c in content:
15	        if c.get("type") == "text":
16	            parts.append(c["text"])
17	        elif isinstance(c, dict) and "text" in c:
18	            parts.append(c["text"])
19	    return "\n".join(parts)
20	
21	for line in open(src, encoding="utf-8"):
22	    d = json.loads(line)
23	    if d.get("type") not in ("user", "assistant"):
24	        continue
25	    msg = d.get("message") or {}
26	    ts = d.get("timestamp", "")
27	    content = msg.get("content")
28	    if d["type"] == "user":
29	        if isinstance(content, str):
30	            out += [f"## User  ({ts})", "", content, ""]
31	            continue
32	        for c in content or []:
33	            if c.get("type") == "text":
34	                out += [f"## User  ({ts})", "", c["text"], ""]
35	            elif c.get("type") == "document":
36	                s = c.get("source", {})
37	                body = s.get("data") if s.get("type") == "text" else json.dumps(s)[:2000]
38	                out += [f"## User - attached document: {c.get('title', '')}  ({ts})", "", "````", body or "", "````", ""]
39	            elif c.get("type") == "tool_result":
40	                body = text_of(c.get("content", ""))
41	                out += [f"**Tool result** ({ts})", "", "````", body, "````", ""]
42	    else:
43	        for c in content or []:
44	            t = c.get("type")
45	            if t == "text" and c["text"].strip():
46	                out += [f"## Claude  ({ts})", "", c["text"], ""]
47	            elif t == "thinking" and c.get("thinking", "").strip():
48	                out += [f"*Claude reasoning ({ts}):*", "", "> " + c["thinking"].replace("\n", "\n> "), ""]
49	            elif t == "tool_use":
50	                out += [f"**Tool call: {c['name']}** ({ts})", "", "````json",
51	                        json.dumps(c.get("input"), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), "````", ""]
52	
53	open(dst, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out))
54	print("wrote", dst)

"""Export one Claude Code session into ai_logs/: raw .jsonl copy + verbatim .md rendering.

Usage (from A10_Group):
    python -I tools/export_session.py <session-id> <file-stem> "<title>"
Example:
    python -I tools/export_session.py 6c37400e-06fc-46b6-b6bf-d83573cd0c9e \
        Sorensen_ClaudeCode_session-procedure_2026-11-18 "Matt Sorensen - Claude Code - ..."

Finds <session-id>.jsonl under any folder in ~/.claude/projects, so it works no matter
which folder Claude Code was launched from. Safe to re-run: it overwrites the same two
files with the fuller transcript. Prints the last timestamp so you can confirm coverage.
"""
import json, shutil, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

sid, stem, title = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
logs = here.parent / "ai_logs"

# A10 Session Procedure

Matt says **"start session"** or **"end session"**; Claude runs the matching checklist and confirms each item. Nothing here is optional.

## Start session
1. **Read the latest handoff** in `handoffs/` (newest `handoff_YYYY-MM-DD.md`) and `memory/a10-master-plan.md`.
2. **Finalize the previous session's transcript.** Re-run its export (command is in the handoff), confirm the printed end time is after that session's last prompt, and mark its row **FINAL** in `ai_logs/SESSION_REGISTRY.md`.
3. **Register this session.** Add a PARTIAL row with this session's id (the folder name in Claude's scratchpad path, or the newest `.jsonl` in `~/.claude/projects/...`), date, and file stem.
4. **Verify against the folder,** not the checkboxes: files the handoff says exist do exist; the notebook was last saved after the last Run All.
5. **Report in 5 lines or fewer:** where we are, schedule vs. plan, first action, any open issue. Then wait for Matt.

## End session
1. **Update `memory/a10-master-plan.md`:** checkboxes plus one dated status-log line.
2. **Update `README.md`** file inventory for any new or renamed file.
3. **Write the handoff** `handoffs/handoff_YYYY-MM-DD.md` (Markdown, never .txt) from the template below. If a second session runs the same day, append `-2`.
4. **Export this session's transcript:**
   `python -I tools/export_session.py <session-id> <stem> "<title>"`
   Stem format: `Sorensen_ClaudeCode_<topic>_<date>`. Leave its registry row PARTIAL; the next session start finalizes it.
5. **Remind Matt** to save any claude.ai chats about A10 into `ai_logs/` verbatim, and add their rows to the registry.
6. **Confirm** with a list of the files written. A Claude-written summary of a conversation is never a substitute for the transcript.

- ...

- ...

## Open issues / risks
- ...

2. ...
```

Last night's transcript is now fully exported, and there's a start and end procedure in place so this shouldn't happen again.

**Re-export.** The transcript in `ai_logs/` now covers the whole session through 11:30 PM on Nov 17, including your final prompt. The `.md` grew from 86 KB to 268 KB, and the raw `.jsonl` from 857 KB to 11.3 MB.

**Why it went wrong.** An export made during a session always misses that session's last turns, and nothing scheduled a second export. On top of that, a summary .txt got written in place of a handoff. The procedure below fixes both.

**How it works now** ([SESSION_PROCEDURE.md](../A10_Group/SESSION_PROCEDURE.md)):
- **When you say "end session":**
  - I update the plan and the README.
  - I write a Markdown handoff to `handoffs/handoff_YYYY-MM-DD.md` using a fixed template: where we stopped, decisions, key numbers, open issues and first actions.
  - I export the transcript and remind you to save any claude.ai chats.

Yes, it can be trimmed. Most of the clutter came from me, mainly the files I added last session for the procedure and the overlapping logs. Here's what's there and whether each piece is needed.

**What the assignment requires in the zip:** data, the Data Receipt (already in the notebook), notebooks, every AI conversation (full and unedited, one file per conversation), the report and deck, and a README. Everything else is working support for us.

| Item | Needed? | Proposal |
|---|---|---|
| `data/`, `notebooks/`, `report/`, `deck/` | Yes | Keep. The empty ones get filled later. |
| `README.md` | Yes (required) | Keep. Absorb the session registry into its `ai_logs` section. |
| Each conversation saved as both `.jsonl` and `.md` | Partly | Two files per conversation breaks the "one file per conversation" rule, and the 11 MB `.jsonl` can't be read by a person. Keep the `.md` as the conversation file and move the `.jsonl` into `ai_logs/raw/` as proof the transcript is unedited. |
| The two `.txt` summaries | No | They're Claude-written summaries and the transcripts already contain everything in them. Delete. |
| `ai_logs/SESSION_REGISTRY.md` | No | Fold into the README. |
| `memory/a10-master-plan.md` + `SESSION_PROCEDURE.md` + `handoffs/` | Overlapping | Combine into **one root file, `PLAN.md`**: the checklist, the status log, a "Handoff" section rewritten at each session end, and the short start/end procedure. You'd have one Markdown file to open when resuming instead of three places. |
| `tools/` with 2 scripts | Overkill | Merge them into one `tools/export_session.py`. |

├── README.md        required: every file + owner, AI log list
├── PLAN.md          plan, status, handoff, session procedure
├── data/raw, data/clean

├── ai_logs/         one .md per conversation
│   └── raw/         .jsonl originals

```

"""Export one Claude Code session into ai_logs/: verbatim .md rendering + raw .jsonl original.

Usage (from A10_Group):
    python -I tools/export_session.py <session-id> <file-stem> "<title>"
Writes:
    ai_logs/<file-stem>.md        the conversation file (user, Claude, tool calls, tool results, in order)
    ai_logs/raw/<file-stem>.jsonl the untouched original, as proof the .md is unedited

Finds <session-id>.jsonl under any folder in ~/.claude/projects, so it works no matter which
folder Claude Code was launched from. Safe to re-run: it overwrites both files with the fuller
transcript. Prints the covered time range so you can confirm the last prompt is included.
"""
import json, shutil, sys
from pathlib import Path

sid, stem, title = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
logs = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "ai_logs"
hits = list((Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects").glob(f"*/{sid}.jsonl"))
if len(hits) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"Expected exactly one transcript for {sid}, found {len(hits)}: {hits}")
src = hits[0]
(logs / "raw").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
shutil.copyfile(src, logs / "raw" / f"{stem}.jsonl")


def text_of(content):
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    return "\n".join(c["text"] for c in content if isinstance(c, dict) and "text" in c)


out = [f"# {title}", "",
       f"Source: Claude Code session `{sid}`; raw original at `ai_logs/raw/{stem}.jsonl`.",
       "Rendered verbatim: user messages, attached documents, Claude replies and reasoning, tool calls "
       "and tool results, in order. Internal harness records (request metadata, file snapshots) are "
       "omitted here but present in the raw file.", ""]
ts, users = [], 0
for line in open(src, encoding="utf-8"):
    d = json.loads(line)
    if d.get("timestamp"):
        ts.append(d["timestamp"])
    if d.get("type") not in ("user", "assistant"):
        continue
    t0 = d.get("timestamp", "")
    content = (d.get("message") or {}).get("content")
    if d["type"] == "user":
        if isinstance(content, str):
            out += [f"## User  ({t0})", "", content, ""]
            users += 1
            continue
        for c in content or []:
            kind = c.get("type")
            if kind == "text":
                out += [f"## User  ({t0})", "", c["text"], ""]
                users += 1
            elif kind == "document":
                s = c.get("source", {})
                body = s.get("data") if s.get("type") == "text" else json.dumps(s)[:2000]
                out += [f"## User - attached document: {c.get('title', '')}  ({t0})", "", "````", body or "", "````", ""]
            elif kind == "tool_result":
                out += [f"**Tool result** ({t0})", "", "````", text_of(c.get("content", "")), "````", ""]
    else:
        for c in content or []:
            kind = c.get("type")
            if kind == "text" and c["text"].strip():
                out += [f"## Claude  ({t0})", "", c["text"], ""]
            elif kind == "thinking" and c.get("thinking", "").strip():
                out += [f"*Claude reasoning ({t0}):*", "", "> " + c["thinking"].replace("\n", "\n> "), ""]
            elif kind == "tool_use":
                out += [f"**Tool call: {c['name']}** ({t0})", "", "````json",
                        json.dumps(c.get("input"), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), "````", ""]

(logs / f"{stem}.md").write_text("\n".join(out), encoding="utf-8")
print(f"wrote   ai_logs/{stem}.md  and  ai_logs/raw/{stem}.jsonl")
print(f"covers  {min(ts)}  to  {max(ts)}  (UTC)   user turns: {users}")

"""Export one Claude Code session into ai_logs/: raw .jsonl copy + verbatim .md rendering.

Usage (from A10_Group):
    python -I tools/export_session.py <session-id> <file-stem> "<title>"
Example:
    python -I tools/export_session.py 6c37400e-06fc-46b6-b6bf-d83573cd0c9e \
        Sorensen_ClaudeCode_session-procedure_2026-11-18 "Matt Sorensen - Claude Code - ..."

Finds <session-id>.jsonl under any folder in ~/.claude/projects, so it works no matter
which folder Claude Code was launched from. Safe to re-run: it overwrites the same two
files with the fuller transcript. Prints the last timestamp so you can confirm coverage.
"""
import json, shutil, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

sid, stem, title = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
logs = here.parent / "ai_logs"
hits = list((Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects").glob(f"*/{sid}.jsonl"))
if len(hits) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"Expected exactly one transcript for {sid}, found {len(hits)}: {hits}")
src = hits[0]

shutil.copyfile(src, logs / f"{stem}.jsonl")
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(here / "export_transcript.py"),
                str(src), str(logs / f"{stem}.md"), title], check=True)

ts, users = [], 0
for line in open(src, encoding="utf-8"):
    d = json.loads(line)
    if d.get("timestamp"):
        ts.append(d["timestamp"])
    if d.get("type") == "user":
        c = d["message"]["content"]
        if isinstance(c, str) or any(x.get("type") == "text" for x in c):
            users += 1
print(f"source  {src}")
print(f"covers  {min(ts)}  to  {max(ts)}  (UTC)   user turns: {users}")

A10 team project (Matt + one colleague, worked as individual until Phase 7), due **Fri Dec 4, 2026, 3:30 PM**, 120 pts. Plan agreed 2026-11-17. This file is the single source of truth for plan, status, and session handoff.

Consolidated folder: plan, handoff, procedure, and AI-log registry now in PLAN.md and README.md; summary .txt logs deleted; raw .jsonl in ai_logs/raw/; one export script. Next: Phase 2 step 9.

A10 team project (Matt + one colleague, worked as individual until Phase 7), due **Fri Dec 4, 2026, 3:30 PM**, 120 pts. Plan agreed 2026-11-17. This file is the single source of truth for plan, status, and session handoff.

Contents: [Handoff](#handoff) · [Session procedure](#session-procedure) · [Direction](#direction) · [Plan and status](#plan-and-status) · [Status log](#status-log)

## Handoff
*Rewritten at every session end. Read this first when resuming.*

**Last updated:** 2026-11-18 (session 6c37400e, in progress)
**Where we stopped:** Phase 2, step 9 (all-field univariate profile) not started. **Schedule:** on track (Phase 2 due Nov 21).
**Done last session:** session b61e1644 transcript fully re-exported; session start/end procedure created; folder structure consolidated (this file replaces memory/, handoffs/, SESSION_PROCEDURE.md, SESSION_REGISTRY.md; summary .txt logs deleted; raw .jsonl moved to ai_logs/raw/).
**Open issues:** none blocking.
**First actions next session:** run Start checklist (below); then step 9 with the Ch 6 skill, cells added after notebook §2.
**Finalize previous transcript with:**
`python -I tools/export_session.py 6c37400e-06fc-46b6-b6bf-d83573cd0c9e Sorensen_ClaudeCode_session-procedure_2026-11-18 "Matt Sorensen - Claude Code - A10 resume check, transcript re-export, session procedure, folder cleanup (2026-11-18)"`

## Session procedure
Matt says **"start session"** or **"end session"**; Claude runs the matching checklist and confirms each item.

**Start session**
1. Read the Handoff above.
2. Finalize the previous session's transcript with the command in the Handoff. Confirm the printed end time is after that session's last prompt, then mark it FINAL in the README's AI conversations table.
3. Add this session to the README table as PARTIAL (session id = folder name in Claude's scratchpad path).
4. Check the folder, not the checkboxes: files the Handoff names exist; notebook saved after its last Run All.
5. Report in 5 lines or fewer: where we are, schedule, first action, open issues. Then wait for Matt.

**End session**
1. Update checkboxes and add one dated Status log line below.
2. Rewrite the Handoff section above (including the finalize command for this session).
3. Update the README file inventory and AI conversations table.
4. Export this session: `python -I tools/export_session.py <session-id> <stem> "<title>"` (stem: `Sorensen_ClaudeCode_<topic>_<date>`). It stays PARTIAL until the next start finalizes it.
5. Remind Matt to save any claude.ai chats about A10 into `ai_logs/` verbatim.
6. List the files written. A Claude-written summary never replaces a transcript.

## Direction
*Agreed 2026-11-17; details in `report/A10_purpose_contract_FROZEN_2026-11-17.md`.*
- Pre-release profitability screen, predictive path with explanatory layer. Decision owner: financier/streamer acquisitions head (flag / review / pass), financing stage.

- Optional, not obtained: TMDB credits file (actor star power).

content.text:
I've restructured the folder as agreed, with the raw `.jsonl` files kept in `ai_logs/raw/`. I removed 7 files and 2 folders and didn't change the data, notebook or report files.

```
A10_Group/
├── README.md        file inventory + AI conversations table (with FINAL/PARTIAL status)
├── PLAN.md          handoff (top) · session procedure · direction · checklist · status log
├── ai_logs/         one .md per conversation (3 so far)
│   └── raw/         original .jsonl for each Claude Code session
├── data/raw/        3 CSVs, untouched
├── data/clean/
├── notebooks/       Sorensen-A10.ipynb
├── report/          problem scan, frozen Purpose Contract
├── deck/
└── tools/export_session.py
```

**What changed:**
- **One file to resume from.** [PLAN.md](../A10_Group/PLAN.md) opens with the **Handoff** section, which says where we stopped and what comes first next session. That section gets rewritten at each session end, so separate handoff files are no longer needed.
  - It replaces the old plan file, `SESSION_PROCEDURE.md` and the `handoffs/` folder.
  - The checklist content is all still there, including the logged AI correction and the key numbers.
- **The conversation list moved into the README.** [README.md](../A10_Group/README.md) now lists every AI conversation, with its file and its FINAL or PARTIAL status. That's where the zip's file-and-owner list has to be anyway.
- **The two summary .txt files are deleted.** Everything in them is in the full transcripts.
- **The two export scripts are now one.** It saves the `.md` to `ai_logs/` and the `.jsonl` to `ai_logs/raw/`. I tested it by re-exporting last night's session, and the output matched the earlier export line for line (3,883 lines).
- **My memory notes now point to PLAN.md.** They also say not to create new tracking files, so this sprawl shouldn't come back.

The old `.md` transcripts still mention file names that no longer exist, such as `SESSION_PROCEDURE.md`. That's expected: they're the unedited record of what happened, so they stay as they are.

Next is Phase 2, step 9: the all-field univariate profile.

So plan.md contains the master plan and also the handoff content for each session stop and start of next session? 
Is the readme.md a project requirement?

Yes to both.

**PLAN.md** holds the master plan and the handoff, in separate sections:
- **Handoff (at the top):** where we stopped, open issues, first actions, and the command to finalize the last transcript. It's rewritten at every session end, so it always describes the latest stop rather than building up a history.
- **Session procedure:** the start and end checklists.
- **Direction, plan and status:** the locked decisions and the 32-step checklist.
- **Status log (at the bottom):** one dated line per session. This is the running history. The full detail is in the transcripts in `ai_logs/`.

When you resume, you only need the top section. When you ask "where are we on the plan?", the checklist answers it.

**README.md is required.** The rubric's 5-point Project folder criterion asks for "a README that lists every file and its main owner (Section 16.3)." The planning chat also noted that the team names on the README have to match the course roster, along with page 1 of the report and slide 1. So the `[colleague name]` placeholder needs to be filled in before packaging.

This is why the AI conversations list went into the README rather than a separate file: the README already has to list every file, transcripts included.
OK, do you recommend we test this now by closing this session, then starting a new session?

Yes. It's a cheap test, and a good time for it, since nothing is in progress. It checks the two things that went wrong last time: whether a new session picks up from the handoff, and whether the finalize step captures this session's last turns.

**How to run it:**
1. Say **"end session"** here. I'll run the end checklist: update PLAN.md (status line and handoff), update the README, export this transcript, and list the files.
2. Close this session and open a new Claude Code session **in the same VS Code workspace**. My memory notes are tied to the `A7` folder this session was launched from. If you open `A10_Group` as the workspace instead, the new session won't see them and won't know the procedure.
3. In the new session, say **"start session"**.

**What a pass looks like:**
- It reads the Handoff without being pointed to it.
- It re-exports this session's transcript, shows an end time after your "end session" prompt, and marks the transcript FINAL in the README.
- It gives a status report of 5 lines or fewer, naming Phase 2, step 9 as the next step.

If it has to ask where things are, or skips the re-export, the test failed and we fix the procedure before going further.

Say "end session" when you're ready.

# A10 Plan, Status, and Handoff

A10 team project (Matt + one colleague, worked as individual until Phase 7), due **Fri Dec 4, 2026, 3:30 PM**, 120 pts. Plan agreed 2026-11-17. This file is the single source of truth for plan, status, and session handoff.

Contents: [Handoff](#handoff) · [Session procedure](#session-procedure) · [Direction](#direction) · [Plan and status](#plan-and-status) · [Status log](#status-log)

## Handoff
*Rewritten at every session end. Read this first when resuming.*

**Last updated:** 2026-11-18 (session 6c37400e, in progress)
**Where we stopped:** Phase 2, step 9 (all-field univariate profile) not started. **Schedule:** on track (Phase 2 due Nov 21).
**Done last session:** session b61e1644 transcript fully re-exported; session start/end procedure created; folder structure consolidated (this file replaces memory/, handoffs/, SESSION_PROCEDURE.md, SESSION_REGISTRY.md; summary .txt logs deleted; raw .jsonl moved to ai_logs/raw/).
**Open issues:** none blocking.
**First actions next session:** run Start checklist (below); then step 9 with the Ch 6 skill, cells added after notebook §2.
**Finalize previous transcript with:**
`python -I tools/export_session.py 6c37400e-06fc-46b6-b6bf-d83573cd0c9e Sorensen_ClaudeCode_session-procedure_2026-11-18 "Matt Sorensen - Claude Code - A10 resume check, transcript re-export, session procedure, folder cleanup (2026-11-18)"`

## Session procedure
Matt says **"start session"** or **"end session"**; Claude runs the matching checklist and confirms each item.

**Start session**
1. Read the Handoff above.
2. Finalize the previous session's transcript with the command in the Handoff. Confirm the printed end time is after that session's last prompt, then mark it FINAL in the README's AI conversations table.
3. Add this session to the README table as PARTIAL (session id = folder name in Claude's scratchpad path).
4. Check the folder, not the checkboxes: files the Handoff names exist; notebook saved after its last Run All.
5. Report in 5 lines or fewer: where we are, schedule, first action, open issues. Then wait for Matt.

**End session**
1. Update checkboxes and add one dated Status log line below.
2. Rewrite the Handoff section above (including the finalize command for this session).
3. Update the README file inventory and AI conversations table.
4. Export this session: `python -I tools/export_session.py <session-id> <stem> "<title>"` (stem: `Sorensen_ClaudeCode_<topic>_<date>`). It stays PARTIAL until the next start finalizes it.
5. Remind Matt to save any claude.ai chats about A10 into `ai_logs/` verbatim.
6. List the files written. A Claude-written summary never replaces a transcript.

## Direction
*Agreed 2026-11-17; details in `report/A10_purpose_contract_FROZEN_2026-11-17.md`.*
- Pre-release profitability screen, predictive path with explanatory layer. Decision owner: financier/streamer acquisitions head (flag / review / pass), financing stage.
- Outcome: money-loser = revenue < 2.5× budget (sensitivity 1×/2×/3×). Focal factor: director prior track record. Capacity: top 20%.
- Population: budget ≥ $1M, revenue > 0, released 2000–2023 → 5,766 films (train 2000–15: 4,145 / test 2016–19: 1,086 / stress 2020–23: 535).
- Data: `TMDB_movie_dataset_v11.csv` (1.54M rows; ODC-By 1.0), `rotten_tomatoes_movies.csv` (143,258 rows; CC0), `rotten_tomatoes_movie_reviews.csv` (1.44M reviews; CC0). Title + year(±1) + runtime join: 83% of 2000–2023 usable films matched 1:1. RT boxOffice vs TMDB revenue Spearman 0.895.
- Optional, not obtained: TMDB credits file (actor star power).

## Plan and status
**Phase 0: Setup (Nov 17–18)**
- [x] 1. Folder layout. Consolidated 2026-11-18 (see README).
- [x] 2. Companion files: rotten_tomatoes_movies.csv added 2026-11-17 (1,206 dup ids).
- [x] 3. AI log started; export procedure in place (`tools/export_session.py`).
- [~] 4. Ownership split DEFERRED: treat A10 as Matt's individual work until Phase 7. Don't raise team coordination unprompted.

**Phase 1: Purpose Contract (Nov 18–19) → 12 pts. COMPLETE**
- [x] 5. Problem scan: `report/A10_problem_scan_2026-11-17.md` (9 candidates; #1 chosen, #2 director premium as rival; #7 marketing and #8 script = reopening evidence).
- [x] 6. Decision statement + red-team. **AI correction logged:** Claude's earlier "usable" filter (votes ≥ 50) selected on a post-release outcome (Spearman 0.48 with log ROI) → dropped. Candidate for the report's required material AI correction.
- [x] 7. Contract FROZEN 2026-11-17 (≥5-pt evidence bar, $1M floor confirmed). Instructor approval not required (Matt confirmed); don't raise again. Changes need a dated amendment in the contract file.

**Phase 2: Data Receipt & Understanding (Nov 19–21) → 8 + 12 pts**
- [x] 8. Data Receipt COMPLETE 2026-11-18 (notebook §2, Run All saved): receipt table, SHA-256 fingerprints, grain check (TMDB 1,019 conflicting dup ids), zero-as-missing budget/revenue, date coverage, population funnel. 43.6% of budget ≥ $1M films lack revenue → S4 triggered. Disposition: FIT WITH CONDITIONS. Rights: academic use only; don't reproduce review text beyond short excerpts; credit TMDB (ODC-By).
- [ ] 9. All-field univariate profile (Ch 6 skill)
- [ ] 10. Build/verify join (2000+, year-validated, 1:1, ~50-pair hand-check with error rate)
- [ ] 11. Test early-review hypothesis (RT reviews dated before release?)
- [ ] 12. Readiness gate (go / narrow), including S4 check via RT boxOffice on revenue-missing films

**Phase 3: Preparation (Nov 21–23) → 8 pts**
- [ ] 13. Cleaning ledger (Ch 7): $1–2 budgets, dup ids, placeholder dates, exclusions, row counts
- [ ] 14. Features with time-order discipline (director/company track record from prior films only, release month, genre…)
- [ ] 15. Reconciliation raw→final + one sensitivity check

**Phase 4: Modeling (Nov 23–25) → 16 pts**
- [ ] 16. Temporal split: train 2000–15, test 2016–19, stress 2020–23
- [ ] 17. Baseline first (genre × budget-tier rule)
- [ ] 18. 1–2 models (logistic; optional tree)
- [ ] 19. Explanatory layer with intervals
- [ ] 20. Capture one material AI correction (error, catch, fix)

**Thanksgiving buffer (Nov 26–29):** light; fresh Run all, catch up

**Phase 5: Evaluation & Decision (Nov 29–Dec 1) → 12 + 8 + 7 pts**
- [ ] 21. Test-period eval vs baseline: losers caught, good films wrongly flagged, calibration, stress period
- [ ] 22. Decision policy + responsible use (selection bias, gross-revenue caveat)
- [ ] 23. Value: fill-in break-even, no invented dollars
- [ ] 24. Verdict (continue/pilot/redirect/satisfice/stop) + reopening evidence
- [ ] 25. Appendix D: independent rebuild of 3–5 key numbers

**Phase 6: Communicate (Dec 1–3) → 7 + 15 pts**
- [ ] 26. Report .docx ≤ 10 main pages; appendices: ledger, join check, App D, AI correction
- [ ] 27. Deck: decision first, 8–10 min, speaker notes, view-only link
- [ ] 28. Traceability: every number → notebook cell

**Phase 7: Package (Dec 3–4 AM) → 5 pts + individual**
- [ ] 29. Fresh Run all on every notebook, save
- [ ] 30. Zip: data, notebooks, all AI conversations (every README row FINAL), report + deck, README (files + owners)
- [ ] 31. Individual: AI Disclosure (10 pts), role statement, workload calibration
- [ ] 32. Both members upload identical zip; target Thu Dec 3 night

**Critical path:** Phases 1–4 done by Nov 25. If behind, cut 2nd model and early-buzz feature first, never evaluation or Appendix D.
**Standing rules:** raw data untouched; contract frozen before modeling; no post-release inputs; export every AI session; narrate in the notebook; Matt must be able to explain every step (final exam draws on the folder).

RT box vs TMDB revenue Spearman 0.895, median ratio 0.55; 1.2% have RT > TMDB (flags bad TMDB revenue). RT director/writer enables director track record.
- 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-18: Phase 1 complete (problem scan, contract frozen on candidate #1). Phase 2 step 8 complete (Data Receipt; FIT WITH CONDITIONS).
- 2026-11-18: Session b61e1644 transcript re-exported in full (to 23:30 Nov 17) → FINAL. Added session start/end procedure. ## Session procedure
Matt says **"start session"** or **"end session"**; Claude runs the matching checklist and confirms each item.

**Workspace rule:** always open `A10_Group` itself as the VS Code workspace before starting Claude Code. Claude's memory for this project is tied to that folder (since 2026-11-18); launching from any other folder starts Claude without it.

**Start session**

2. Finalize the previous session's transcript with the command in the Handoff. Confirm the printed end time is after that session's last prompt, then mark it FINAL in the README's AI conversations table.
3. Add this session to the README table as PARTIAL (session id = folder name in Claude's scratchpad path).
4. Check the folder, not the checkboxes: files the Handoff names exist; notebook saved after its last Run All.
5. Report in 5 lines or fewer: where we are, schedule, first action, open issues. Then wait for Matt.

**End session**
1. Update checkboxes and add one dated Status log line below.
2. Rewrite the Handoff section above (including the finalize command for this session).
3. Update the README file inventory and AI conversations table.
4. Export this session: `python -I tools/export_session.py <session-id> <stem> "<title>"` (stem: `Sorensen_ClaudeCode_<topic>_<date>`). It stays PARTIAL until the next start finalizes it.
5. Remind Matt to save any claude.ai chats about A10 into `ai_logs/` verbatim.
6. List the files written. A Claude-written summary never replaces a transcript.

## Direction
*Agreed 2026-11-17; details in `report/A10_purpose_contract_FROZEN_2026-11-17.md`.*
- Pre-release profitability screen, predictive path with explanatory layer. Decision owner: financier/streamer acquisitions head (flag / review / pass), financing stage.
- Outcome: money-loser = revenue < 2.5× budget (sensitivity 1×/2×/3×). Focal factor: director prior track record. Capacity: top 20%.
- Population: budget ≥ $1M, revenue > 0, released 2000–2023 → 5,766 films (train 2000–15: 4,145 / test 2016–19: 1,086 / stress 2020–23: 535).
- Data: `TMDB_movie_dataset_v11.csv` (1.54M rows; ODC-By 1.0), `rotten_tomatoes_movies.csv` (143,258 rows; CC0), `rotten_tomatoes_movie_reviews.csv` (1.44M reviews; CC0). Title + year(±1) + runtime join: 83% of 2000–2023 usable films matched 1:1. RT boxOffice vs TMDB revenue Spearman 0.895.
- Optional, not obtained: TMDB credits file (actor star power).
